name: doctor
description: Memory (available, kernel pressure, swap), open files and threads against the kernel's limits; the processes holding half of each; findings with remediation. With watch_seconds, samples twice and projects time to each limit from measured growth (use it to catch descriptor or thread leaks).

name: incidents
description: macOS: kernel panics (classified watchdog / GPU memory driver / other), jetsam kills with the largest process, shutdown stalls, and optionally resource-limit reports, from the OS's own crash reports. Linux: OOM kills (machine or cgroup, with memory freed) and hung tasks from the kernel log (journalctl -k).

all.description: Include resource-limit reports (disk writes, CPU, wakeups).

name: fit
description: Whether a GGUF model (a path or an Ollama model name) at a total KV context fits this machine's accelerator and fits right now, with weights and KV bytes from the model's own metadata and the largest context that would fit. Excludes runtime compute buffers.

model.description: Path to a .gguf file (any shard of a split model), or an Ollama model name such as qwen3:8b, read from Ollama's store without asking Ollama. Required unless port is given.

ctx.description: Total tokens of KV cache the runtime will allocate (llama.cpp -c; Ollama num_ctx x OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL).

cache_type.description: KV cache type: f32 f16 bf16 q8_0 q5_1 q5_0 q4_1 q4_0 iq4_nl.

cache_type_v.description: Value cache type when it differs from cache_type.

parallel.description: Parallel sequences (with ubatch, bounds sliding-window caches).

port.description: Instead of model (or with an Ollama model name): the port of a running server on this machine, asked which model it serves. Answers whether that server could take a different context.

name: ports
description: Every listening TCP port with its process, and which model runtime answers there: Ollama (models, loaded models with sizes), llama.cpp (model path, n_ctx, slots, health), ComfyUI, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible. Ports that accept connections but never answer are flagged (a wedged server looks like that). Probes are read-only GETs.

runtimes_only.description: Only ports where a model runtime answers.

name: log
description: Snapshots hearth recorded of this machine, newest first, each with a one-line summary. ports and doctor record one on every full run, so this is the machine's history as hearth saw it. Refer to a snapshot by id or as ~N (N before the latest).

kind.description: Which command's snapshots (default ports). run lists every event of hearth run: starts, readiness, exits, wedges, poisoned backends, give-ups.

name: diff
description: What changed between two recorded snapshots. ports: listeners that appeared or vanished, runtimes that restarted (new pid), stopped answering, changed health or loaded models, and footprint movement. doctor: memory pressure changes, available memory, swap, kernel-wide open files and threads, and per-process open files, threads and CLOSE_WAIT movement (a leak shows as steady growth across snapshots). Defaults to the last two snapshots; run ports or doctor first to record a fresh one.

from.description: Older snapshot: an id from log, ~N, or a tag name (default ~1).

to.description: Newer snapshot (id, ~N or tag) (default ~0, the latest).

name: show
description: One recorded snapshot in full, as it was written (the complete ports, doctor or run report). Use after log or diff to see everything a snapshot holds.

reference.description: An id from log, ~N, or a tag name for N before the latest (default ~0).

name: follow
description: One process, port or server across every recorded snapshot, oldest first: when it appeared, changed state, restarted (new pid), grew, or went away. ports: state and footprint; doctor: open files, threads and CLOSE_WAIT per process (a leak shows as steady growth); run: supervision events.

pattern.description: Part of a process name, pid, address, path or server name; case is ignored.

kind.description: Which snapshots to follow it through (default ports).

all.description: Every snapshot, not only those where something changed.

name: tag
description: Name this moment, like git tag: the latest ports, doctor and run snapshots get the name, are kept past retention, and can be used wherever a snapshot is asked for (diff from, show reference). Tag a healthy state, then diff against it when something goes wrong. Without a name, lists the tags.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits, '-', '_', '.'; starting with a letter.

name: status
description: What hearthd keeps alive: each owned server's name, address, state (starting, ready, waiting, gave_up), pid, restart count and last event (exited, wedged, poisoned, ...). Fails with a clear message when hearthd is not running.

name: restart
description: Ask hearthd to restart one of the servers it owns, now; the restart budget is not charged. Only servers configured under [servers] can be restarted: hearth never touches a process it did not start.

server.description: Server name as in [servers.NAME]; status lists them.

name: stop
description: Ask hearthd to stop one of the servers it owns and keep it down, to free its memory (for example before loading a bigger model). It stays down until start. Only servers configured under [servers]: hearth never touches a process it did not start.

server.description: Server name as in [servers.NAME]; status lists them.

name: start
description: Ask hearthd to start a server it stopped, or one it gave up on after a crash loop.

server.description: Server name as in [servers.NAME]; status lists them.

name: logs
description: The last lines one of hearthd's servers printed (stdout and stderr, across restarts): why it failed to load, what it said before it was found wedged or poisoned.

server.description: Server name as in [servers.NAME]; status lists them.

name: bundle
description: Everything hearth can say about this machine in one document: doctor, ports, incidents, hearthd status, recent supervision events, tags and settings, with secrets redacted. Use it to get the whole picture in one call, or to attach to a bug report. Takes a few seconds (it probes every port).

since.description: Incidents since this time prefix, e.g. 2026-10-14.

name: config
description: Every hearth setting in effect: value, source (built-in or the user's file), and what it means. hearth keeps no numbers in code; use this to see why it waited, retried, restarted or reported something, and which key to change.

filter.description: Only keys containing this, e.g. supervise or deadline.

name: process_memory
description: Memory the kernel charges to processes whose name or path contains a pattern, or to one pid: footprint (includes GPU allocations on Apple Silicon), resident, lifetime peak.
